alt: Paired SL and HL bars for each topic: Foundations 16 at both levels, Ecology 22 and 35, Biodiversity and conservation 13 and 26, Water 12 and 25, Land 8 and 15, Atmosphere and climate change 10 and 23, Natural resources 10 and 18, Human populations and urban systems 9 and 15, plus HL-only lenses of 5, 7 and 5 hours. Content totals 100 hours at SL and 190 at HL, with a 50-hour experimental programme at both levels.
caption: Topics 2, 3, 4 and 6 each gain 13 hours at HL: that is where HL depth sits.

alt: The three Topic 1 concepts, perspectives (3 hours), systems (5 hours) and sustainability (8 hours), run as lines through Topics 2 to 8. Below, the vocabulary to use in every answer: carrying capacity, ecological footprint, environmental value systems and positive or negative feedback.
caption: Topic 1 is the framework for every later topic, not a warm-up.

alt: A core-topic issue such as water scarcity branches to three HL-only lenses: environmental law (5 hours), environmental and ecological economics (7 hours) and environmental ethics (5 hours), each asking a different question of the same issue.
caption: HL lenses re-read content you already know; revise them topic by topic.

alt: A 50-hour bar split into practical work (30 hours), the collaborative sciences project (10 hours, not separately graded) and scientific investigation (10 hours). It feeds the internally assessed individual investigation: draft a testable research question early and check it against the criteria, gather and analyse data, then write an evidence-based report of up to 3,000 words.
caption: A focused research question, set early, saves more marks than any rescue later.
